mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.5 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below $330 billion, indicates supply-side stress, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 AND RSAFS < 330 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk asset valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening demand, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% month-over-month indicates labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for four consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals broad-based supply weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered periods.
